title: GitHub Actions Basics
subtitle: Read, write, and troubleshoot a small CI workflow.
description: Learn how events create workflow runs, how jobs and steps execute, how data crosses job boundaries, and how to keep a first workflow safe and observable.

concepts.name: Workflow
concepts.definition: A YAML file in .github/workflows that defines the events and jobs for one automation.

concepts.name: Workflow run
concepts.definition: One execution of a workflow after a matching event starts it.

concepts.name: Event
concepts.definition: Repository activity, a schedule, or a manual request that GitHub can match against a workflow's on section.

concepts.name: Job
concepts.definition: A group of ordered steps assigned to one runner. Jobs are isolated unless the workflow connects them explicitly.

concepts.name: Runner
concepts.definition: The machine that executes one job's steps. GitHub can host it, or you can register your own machine.

concepts.name: Step
concepts.definition: One ordered command or reusable action inside a job. Steps in the same job share its runner workspace.

concepts.name: Trigger
concepts.definition: The event configuration that decides whether GitHub creates a workflow run. Filters can narrow which matching events count.

concepts.name: Job dependency
concepts.definition: A needs relationship that makes one job wait for selected earlier jobs and exposes their declared outputs.

concepts.name: Artifact
concepts.definition: Files uploaded from a run so another job or a person can download the exact result later.

concepts.name: Cache
concepts.definition: Reusable dependency data stored to make later runs faster. A cache is an optimization, not a build result.

concepts.name: Matrix
concepts.definition: A set of variable combinations that expands one job definition into several related jobs.

concepts.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
concepts.definition: A short-lived token GitHub creates for a job. Its permissions control which repository operations the workflow may perform.

lessons.title: From event to run
lessons.summary: Build the core mental model: an event selects a workflow, jobs go to runners, and steps execute in order.

lessons.title: Write a first CI workflow
lessons.summary: Read a complete workflow file and connect each YAML key to what GitHub will do.

lessons.title: Choose triggers and filters
lessons.summary: Start workflows from repository activity or a manual request, then narrow when they should run.

lessons.title: Connect jobs and data
lessons.summary: Control parallel work with dependencies and choose outputs, artifacts, or caches for different kinds of data.

lessons.title: Make workflows safe and debuggable
lessons.summary: Limit token permissions, treat external values as untrusted, and diagnose failures from trigger to side effect.
